finding: 72% of the street-miles of the Chicago Surface Lines (CSL) network on its 1929 map still carry a CTA bus. 53% of CTA bus street-miles today run on a CSL line, and only 11% lie more than half a mile from one.

ledger.source: Chicago Surface Lines, System of Chicago Surface Lines (1929), scan by the University of Minnesota; CTA GTFS; OpenStreetMap
ledger.units: 535 street-miles of CSL lines (1929 map), 730 of CTA bus routes today
method: Scan georeferenced to the address grid from its margin street numbers (RMS 38 / 30 address units), then by snapping OSM arterials to the red lines; Loop from the map's Central District inset
A street is a CSL line where red ink runs along it on the 1929 map for at least half its length (smoothed over a quarter mile)
Today: Plate II's CTA bus routes (GTFS 2026-09-14) on the street, within 25 address units
Street-miles inside today's city on 40-unit cells, so both roadways of a divided street count once
caveats: A check by eye of 40 + 40 random streets: 33/40 "CSL only" and 39/40 "CTA only" right; shares likely 53%–54% and 72%–77%
The 1929 sheet is the CSL's own system map for riders, a snapshot of its network that year; a few CSL bus lines (dashed) may be missed
Two CSL lines moved by hand to the street the map labels: Congress to Harrison, Leland to Lawrence
91 miles of city streets lie off the sheet (O'Hare area) and are left out; expressways and Lake Shore Drive too
